summary: Review the database, security, live-site compatibility and the screens of the finished accuracy round, and verify every finding

review.lens: Migration, database, security and compatibility with the live site: supabase/migrations/20261119000001_accuracy.sql, tests/sql, sync_upsert_estimate 'locked', price_approvals and quote_number_counters with their RLS, next_quote_number, /api/approvals and /api/approvals/[id], /api/quotes (approvals, counter, consent), ApprovalQueue, lib/server/auth.ts, proxy.ts x-koala-path, /unreachable, lib/server/snapshot.ts, /api/bundle. Reviewed claude/accuracy 587ce69 against origin/claude/daymark 9051b81 and origin/main c0ae5f1. Production (fznkewranivklezxhtsf) was only read, with SELECTs. Worktrees and scratch databases were removed afterwards. The probe outputs and logs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/e9b02a42-cb4a-5aa1-bf7b-e82e27ad6b23/scratchpad/accuracy/revB/database (stack-probe.out, compat-main-with-mig-2.log, compat-main-baseline-2.log, branch-e2e-2.log, revb-probe.test.ts.txt, probe/stack-probe.mjs, safenext-probe.mjs, consent-probe.mts).
checkedOk: PRODUCTION SHAPE: production's schema is the same as a local database built from origin/claude/daymark's migrations. Production lists only 5 migrations in its log, but the comparison still matched. I compared md5 hashes: columns of all 48 public tables and views (each hash equal); every constraint, index, policy and trigger, and every enum label (one hash each, all equal); and every public function body (pg_get_functiondef). sync_upsert_estimate is 8ecf43fe… on both, and is identical to phase2. tg_audit, can_edit_estimate, has_role, auth_role and log_event are also equal. Production runs PG 17.11; local runs 16.15.

Production rows the migration reads are the seed rows. There are 6 active default materials, one per product: cellulose $14.00/bag with coverage 200, and batts $0.75/sq ft. The active set is v1 'seed', with cellulose waste_factor 1.08 inside its 1.00-1.60 bounds. app_settings has no default_state, default_city or quote_number_prefix. On a production-shaped copy the migration adds exactly this: one dense-pack walls row ($14, 122.5), seven batt sizes at $0.75 (none is a default), the walls cell 1.08 [1.00,1.60] in the active set only, ranges from half to twice the cost on all 14 rows (ocsf 0.06-0.24, ccsf 0.235-0.94, cellulose 7-28, blown 19-76, batts 0.375-1.50, air sealing 0.05-0.20), and the prefix 'KN'.

RE-RUN: I ran the migration twice with psql --single-transaction on a daymark copy. Both runs exited 0. The materials row hash (including updated_at) and the coefficient count did not change. A partial state (only the cavity and quotes sections, then the full file) applies cleanly. A forced error at the end of the file leaves nothing behind: no new columns, no price_approvals table.

COMPATIBILITY: I re-ran origin/main's own e2e in a worktree of c0ae5f1 (npm ci; build retried once at the security notice, nothing upgraded). With only 20261119000001_accuracy.sql added: 225 ok, EXIT 0. Without it: 225 ok, EXIT 0, with identical ok lines apart from timestamps. The one console line (ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED on /api/estimates in the offline step) showed up in my with-migration run but not in my baseline. The flow stage's baseline log has it, so it is a timing flake, not the migration.

main receiving 'locked': main's applySyncResult already has a 'locked' case (server doc, status signed, read-only). Main's /api/sync passes the RPC status through. Main's draft schema requires a 2-letter state, so the new null fallback for state is never reached through either app's /api/sync.

main's default-material lookup is active and is_default, and the migration's constraint keeps the new rows from ever being a default. main's findCoefficient picks the walls cell for cellulose walls at the same 1.08, so prices are equal. A phone still on main's engine that is given the new bundle takes the first material per product, and makeBundle sorts the general material first. main's nightly learning ran in its e2e with the walls cell present ('no coefficient moved').

A quote sent by main after the migration (from main's e2e database): number KN-2026-0C9721-v1 (main's hex scheme). It has no consent field, so the new code's consentFor returns the legacy sentence main showed. expires_at is sent_at + 30 days. Counter numbers (4 digits) can never equal main's 6-hex-digit numbers.
model_total_price: the branch now writes the recommended option's model price. main's office list reads it only as the last fallback after signed_price and the selected option's price.

next_quote_number is SECURITY DEFINER with search_path = public, pg_temp. Production's default ACL grants EXECUTE to anon and authenticated at creation, and the migration revokes it from public, anon and authenticated, leaving service_role. quote_number_counters likewise: RLS on, no policies, table owned by postgres, so the definer bypasses RLS. tg_price_approval_guard has a pinned search_path. Both new tables have RLS enabled.

RLS and API probes on a kept branch e2e stack (ports 3530/3531/54730). An estimator PATCHing their own request to approved updates 0 rows, and DELETE updates 0 rows. Crew reads none and an insert is refused (42501). Anon gets 'permission denied for table price_approvals', and anon calling next_quote_number gets 'permission denied'. An API insert forces requested_by to the caller and status to pending (the SQL test also covers another estimator, office below the floor, own request, frozen decisions). Routes: crew and owner POST /api/approvals 403; estimator GET queue 403; estimator PATCH 403; no session 401; malformed body 400.

x-koala-path: proxy.ts always overwrites it. A spoofed '/.//evil.example/x' header on /estimates during an outage still redirects to /unreachable?next=%2Festimates. The header only feeds next= and never decides access.

503 path: with REST down, crew GET /api/approvals returns 503 with no data, no session returns 401, and crew /admin/pricing goes to /unreachable (then /no-access once REST is back). /unreachable reads no data.

npm run test:db passes (10, 20, 30, 31 and 40). The vitest subset (lib/server, safeNext, approvals, support, syncCore, sendChecks) passes: 64 tests. The branch e2e (APP_PORT 3530) gives 319 ok with no console errors.

Claims I verified as true: 'origin/main's e2e passes with only the migration' (225 ok); 'runs twice with no change'; 'a saved range/prefix is kept on a re-run'; 'sync_upsert_estimate same signature, grants authenticated only' (production: postgres, authenticated, service_role, unchanged).

findings.title: Open redirect: /unreachable's 'Try again' sends people to another site for a next= with dot segments (and the same hole in /login, /auth/confirm, /auth/demo)
findings.failureScenario: An attacker sends staff the public link https://<koala>/unreachable?next=/.//evil.example/x, which shows 'Can't reach Koala right now'. Clicking 'Try again' opens evil.example, which can show a fake Koala sign-in page. safeNext only rejects input that starts with '//' or '/\'. It then returns url.pathname after WHATWG normalisation, and normalising '/./', '/x/../' or '/%2e/' turns the path into '//evil.example/x'. The same value goes into LoginForm (router.replace(next) and the magic-link emailRedirectTo /auth/confirm?next=…, whose new URL(next, origin) resolves to https://evil.example/x) and into /auth/demo when demo mode is on. safeNext is unchanged from origin/main, so /login and /auth/confirm already have this hole on the live site. The new /unreachable page is a new public entry point, and the flow stage's claim 'next= same-site only' (flow.json L36, ledger L36) is not true. Expected: every next= ends on this site.
findings.evidence: Probe on the running branch stack (stack-probe.out): unreachable next="/.//evil.example/x" -> Try again href="//evil.example/x" -> browser goes to http://evil.example/x. Same result for "/a/..//evil.example/x" and "/%2e//evil.example/x". Only "//evil.example/x" -> "/" is caught (the one input the tests use). Plain node with the same function: safeNext('/.//evil.com') -> '//evil.com'; safeNext('/x/../\\evil.com') -> '//evil.com'. Also new URL('//evil.example/x','https://koala.example').href is 'https://evil.example/x'. diff of lib/safeNext.ts against origin/main: identical.
findings.suggestedFix: In safeNext, check the normalised result as well as the input: after parsing, return the fallback when url.pathname starts with '//' or '/\'. Alternatively build the result as '/' + url.pathname.replace(/^\/+/, ''). Add test cases '/.//evil.com', '/a/..//evil.com', '/%2e//evil.com', '/./\\evil.com' to lib/safeNext.test.ts and lib/server/sessionState.test.ts.

findings.title: An owner approval still covers a quote after line changes push its margin below the floor (to -41%); the approval is not bound to the cost
findings.failureScenario: An approval is matched on tier, exact price, model price and decidedRole only (approvalCovers). The model price ignores line overrides: with line overrides, modelPrice is replaced by the pure-model price (engine.ts line 87). After the owner approves a price, the estimator can change line quantities or hours (with a reason and a deviation note, which they write themselves). That raises the job cost while the price and model price stay the same, so the old approval still covers the send. In addition, for a below_floor problem approvalCovers accepts any owner-decided approval and never checks a.belowFloor. So an approval the owner gave for an above-floor, over-the-limit request also covers a send that is now below the floor. Example (seed fixture): (A) the owner approves Good $3,500 at a 7.2% margin; labor hours are then quadrupled; the cost goes from $3,249 to $4,938, the margin to -41.1%, and the send is still allowed. (B) the owner approves Good $4,500 (over the limit, 27.8% margin, not below the floor); hours are tripled; the margin drops to 0.9%, below the 25% floor, and the send is still allowed. Expected: a quote below the floor goes out only at a margin the owner actually approved. flow.json says 'if pricing changes between the approval and the send, the estimator asks again', which does not hold for line changes.
findings.evidence: Scratch vitest in my worktree (saved as revb-probe.test.ts.txt), calling priceEstimate and canSendQuote exactly as /api/quotes line 142 does: 'A below-floor approval: owner approved 3500 model 5420 cost 3249.2 margin 7.2% problem below_floor | labor hours x4 -> price 3500 model 5420 cost 4938 margin -41.1% problem below_floor | send allowed with the old approval: true' and 'B over-limit approval: owner approved 4500 model 5420 cost 3249.2 margin 27.8% problem over_limit | labor hours x3 -> price 4500 model 5420 cost 4458 margin 0.9% problem below_floor | send allowed with the old approval: true'. The approval reuse tests (support.test.ts 'an approved price can be sent…') vary price, model price, tier, status and role, but not the cost.
findings.suggestedFix: Store the option's loaded cost (or its margin) on price_approvals, as an additive column; the server already has it in checkApprovalRequest's problem. In approvalCovers, require the current loadedCost to be no higher than the approved one, within a cent, so the margin is never lower than approved. For a below_floor problem, also require a.belowFloor. Add tests for line-override hours and quantities after an approval, and for an over_limit owner approval used on a below-floor option.

findings.title: Removing the business-profile gate on production's real settings makes every send fail (consent needs default_state, which production does not have) and would print the PLACEHOLDER warranty
findings.failureScenario: The owner decided that nothing blocks sending for missing profile details. Today only the L30 gate (businessProfileGaps -> 409 setup_incomplete) keeps two things from happening on production. (1) /api/quotes builds the consent with esignConsent(profileValue(settingRows, 'default_state')). Production's app_settings has no default_state; no migration seeds it, and with no profile form nobody will set it. esignConsent('') throws 'Not a US state: ', so with the gate removed every POST /api/quotes returns 500 and no quote can be sent. (2) Production's warranty_text value is 'Workmanship warranty — PLACEHOLDER, owner to replace.' (only the gate stops it). Without the gate it prints on the page, the PDF and the email, instead of 'Limited lifetime warranty'. (The seeded company name and terms 'Koala Insulation of Newark' are review A's DOC-1 and DOC-6, not repeated here. Phone and license are already left off when null in the PDF, email and /q, so that part is fine.)
findings.evidence: Production, read-only: select key from app_settings gives 21 keys, with no default_state, default_city or quote_number_prefix. warranty_text is the PLACEHOLDER value above; branding is {phone: null, license: null, company: 'Koala Insulation of Newark'}. consent-probe.mts, using the branch's lib/quotes/consent.ts with production's rows: 'THROWS: Not a US state: '. Call site: route.ts line 189, consent: esignConsent(profileValue(settingRows, 'default_state')).
findings.suggestedFix: When the gate is removed, give the consent a wording that does not need a state (for example ESIGN Act only), or take the state from a source production has (the property's state or shop_address), and never throw on a missing state. Make the warranty 'Limited lifetime warranty' when warranty_text is empty or holds a placeholder. Preferably also add a conditional, additive migration update that replaces the seeded warranty only where it still equals the seeded PLACEHOLDER text (hard rule 2). Add a send-route test with production's exact app_settings rows.

findings.title: Approval requests can be written straight to the database with a made-up model price and below_floor flag, and the owner's queue shows them as fact
findings.failureScenario: The price_approvals_ask policy lets an estimator INSERT through PostgREST (Supabase's anon key plus their session token). Only the role, requested_by, pending status and can_edit_estimate are checked. price, model_price and below_floor come from the caller, and the server's checks (checkApprovalRequest: price matches the server price, approval needed, which kind) are skipped. Example: an estimator posts {tier: good, price: 3500, model_price: 5420 (the true value), below_floor: false} for a price that is actually below the floor. The owner's queue shows 'Good: $3,500, 35% below the model price of $5,420' without the 'Below the floor margin' tag. If the owner approves, approvalCovers (below_floor plus owner) lets the below-floor price go out, although the owner was told it was above the floor. With a made-up model price the approval cannot be used, but it still puts misleading numbers in front of the decider. Expected: what the decider sees is computed by the server.
findings.evidence: stack-probe.out: 'estimator direct insert, made-up model price and below_floor=false: 201 [{"price":1001.00,"model_price":1000.00,"below_floor":false,"status":"pending",…}]' (the trigger reset status and requested_by, but kept model_price and below_floor). The owner's GET /api/approvals then lists it: {"price":1001,"modelPrice":1000,"belowFloor":false,"status":"pending","note":"probe"}.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the server the only writer of what was asked. Either revoke INSERT on price_approvals from authenticated and insert from POST /api/approvals with the service role after checkApprovalRequest (requested_by = profile.userId), or insert through a SECURITY DEFINER RPC that prices the request. Alternatively, have the queue and PATCH recompute below_floor and the model price from the estimate before offering Approve.

findings.title: The test databases re-grant the counter to every signed-in user, so test:db and the e2e do not match production's grants
findings.failureScenario: 01_grants.sql runs after all migrations and grants EXECUTE on all functions and ALL on all tables to authenticated. In every npm run test:db and scripts/e2e.sh stack, any signed-in user can call next_quote_number and use up quote numbers, and can select quote_number_counters (RLS returns nothing). Production is different: its default ACL applies at creation and the migration's revoke holds. The 40_accuracy test only passes because it re-runs the migration before checking the grants, and the e2e stack never checks them. A future migration that forgets the revoke would not be caught.
findings.evidence: On the kept branch e2e database: select has_function_privilege('authenticated','next_quote_number(int)','execute') returns t, and has_table_privilege('authenticated','quote_number_counters','select') returns t. Probe: owner POST /rest/v1/rpc/next_quote_number {year: 2026} returns 200 with 2, and the counter moved to 2.
findings.suggestedFix: Copy Supabase's real behaviour in the test stub: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT … TO anon, authenticated, service_role in 00_supabase_stub.sql, before the migrations, and drop the after-the-fact grants in 01_grants.sql (keep the audit_log revoke). Then add a grant check to the e2e.

findings.title: Every franchise's database gets the 'KN' quote prefix, and under the new decision there is no form to change it
findings.failureScenario: The migration seeds quote_number_prefix 'KN' ('the one quotes already carry'). Once the business profile form goes away (owner decision), each new franchise's quotes read KN-2026-0001-v1 and the app offers no way to change that. If 'KN' stands for this franchise (Koala Newark), it is franchise-specific text in code (hard rule 3). I could not confirm what KN stands for.
findings.evidence: Migration lines 125-127 insert ('quote_number_prefix', '"KN"'). quotes.json ownerQuestions: 'Quote number prefix KN, the one quotes already carry; each franchise sets its own on the Business profile page'. That page goes away under the new decision.
findings.suggestedFix: Owner call: either seed a neutral prefix for new databases (keeping 'KN' only where quotes already carry it, for example when there are rows in quotes), or keep one way to set the prefix.

findings.title: scripts/e2e.sh fails for an E2E_DB_NAME with capital letters
findings.failureScenario: E2E_DB_NAME=koala_revB_db (the name this review was given): 'create database $DB_NAME' is unquoted, so Postgres creates koala_revb_db, but E2E_DB_URL keeps koala_revB_db. The run stops at once with exit 2.
findings.evidence: branch-e2e-1.log (first attempt): 'psql: error: connection to server on socket "/tmp/kpg/.s.PGSQL.5499" failed: FATAL:  database "koala_revB_db" does not exist', EXIT 2. With E2E_DB_NAME=koala_revb_db the same run gives 319 ok.
findings.suggestedFix: Quote the identifier in both psql commands ("$DB_NAME" inside double quotes in the SQL), or lowercase DB_NAME before building E2E_DB_URL.

verdicts.reproduction: My own worktree at 587ce69, my own stack (built with npx next build; the security notice appeared once and the build carried on; app on 3530, PostgREST on 3531, mock on 54730, database koala_revb_db). (1) Plain function: node --experimental-strip-types sn.mts printed "/.//evil.example/x" -> "//evil.example/x", "/a/..//evil.example/x" -> "//evil.example/x", "/%2e//evil.example/x" -> "//evil.example/x", "/./\\evil.com" -> "//evil.com", "/%2e%2e//evil.com" -> "//evil.com", and only "//evil.com" and "/\\evil.com" -> "/". new URL(result, 'https://koala.example/...') resolves each of them to https://evil.example/x. (2) Running page: curl /unreachable?next=%2F.%2F%2Fevil.example%2Fx returned <a href="//evil.example/x" ...>Try again. (3) Playwright (b1.cjs, evil.example answered by a route stub): '"/.//evil.example/x" | page: Can't reach Koala right now | after Try again: http://evil.example/x | EVIL fake Koala sign-in'. The same happens for '/a/..//evil.example/x' and '/%2e//evil.example/x'. Only '//evil.example/x' ends on localhost. (4) /login?next=/.//evil.example/x renders LoginForm with next "//evil.example/x" in the RSC payload. LoginForm then calls router.replace(next) after the code is verified, and puts the same value in emailRedirectTo /auth/confirm?next=. /auth/confirm does NextResponse.redirect(new URL('//evil.example/x', origin)), which goes to https://evil.example/x. The e2e mock has no OTP verify endpoint, so I checked /auth/confirm and /auth/demo in the code only. git diff origin/main -- lib/safeNext.ts is empty, so /login and /auth/confirm on the live site have the same hole.
verdicts.reasoning: safeNext checks only the raw input for a leading '//' or '/\'. It then returns the WHATWG-normalised pathname, and that normalisation turns dot segments into a leading '//'. No owner decision or hard rule makes this intended. The ledger and flow.json claim 'next= same-site only' / 'next=<same-site path>' is false. The new public /unreachable page is a fresh, zero-click-to-render entry point for phishing staff. I kept high rather than blocker: no token or session leaks, it is a redirect that helps phishing, and the live site already has it on /login.
verdicts.fixSpec: lib/safeNext.ts: accept `next: unknown` and return the fallback for anything that is not a string. After `new URL(next, HERE)`, also return the fallback when `url.pathname` starts with '//' or '/\' (keep the origin check). Optionally collapse the result with '/' + url.pathname.replace(/^[\/\\]+/, ''). No caller changes are needed: /unreachable, /login, /auth/confirm, /auth/demo and lib/server/sessionState.unreachableHref all go through it. Tests that fail before and pass after: lib/safeNext.test.ts, where safeNext of '/.//evil.com', '/a/..//evil.com', '/%2e//evil.com', '/%2e%2e//evil.com', '/./\\evil.com' and '/x/../\\evil.com' are each '/', and safeNext(['/a','/b']) is '/'. lib/server/sessionState.test.ts: unreachableHref('/.//evil.com') === '/unreachable?next=%2F'. Optionally add an e2e step: /unreachable?next=%2F.%2F%2Fevil.example%2Fx, where Try again has href '/'.

verdicts.reproduction: In my worktree I copied the reviewer's probe to lib/pricing/zz-verify-b2.test.ts and ran npx vitest run lib/pricing/zz-verify-b2.test.ts --silent=false (the file was removed afterwards). It calls priceEstimate and canSendQuote(role, options, settings, approvals) the same way app/api/quotes/route.ts lines 139-140 do. Output: 'A below-floor approval: owner approved 3500 model 5420 cost 3249.2 margin 7.2% problem below_floor | labor hours x4 -> price 3500 model 5420 cost 4938 margin -41.1% problem below_floor | send allowed with the old approval: true' and 'B over-limit approval: owner approved 4500 model 5420 cost 3249.2 margin 27.8% problem over_limit | labor hours x3 -> price 4500 model 5420 cost 4458 margin 0.9% problem below_floor | send allowed with the old approval: true'. The code path is real. lib/sync/draft.ts lineOverrideSchema accepts hours (line 34) and the server prices the synced draft. engine.ts line 87 sets modelPrice to the pure-model price whenever there are line overrides. policy.ts lines 93-95: approvalCovers compares only status, tier, price and modelPrice, and for below_floor it checks decidedRole === 'owner' without looking at a.belowFloor. The only other gate is the deviation note (unacknowledgedFlags), which the estimator writes themselves.
verdicts.reasoning: The floor-margin rule (only the owner may send below the floor) breaks for a realistic sequence: approval first, then the estimator adjusts labor or quantities, then send. The owner approved a 7.2% margin and the customer gets a -41% job. In case B the owner never knew the price was below the floor at all. flow.json line 55 says 'if pricing changes between the approval and the send, the estimator asks again', and that does not hold for cost changes. No OD covers this. No existing test varies the cost (policy and support tests vary only price, model price, tier, status and role).
verdicts.fixSpec: 1) Migration (additive, append to supabase/migrations/20261119000001_accuracy.sql or a new file): alter table price_approvals add column if not exists loaded_cost numeric(12,2). Leave it nullable so origin/main is unaffected, and add it to the guard trigger's frozen-field list. 2) lib/pricing/policy.ts: add loadedCost to the PolicyProblem base (o.loadedCost) and to PriceApproval. In approvalCovers, return false when a.loadedCost is null/undefined or p.loadedCost > a.loadedCost + 0.005, and for kind 'below_floor' also require a.belowFloor. 3) app/api/approvals/route.ts POST: insert loaded_cost: problem.loadedCost. lib/quotes/approvals.ts: APPROVAL_COLUMNS and approvalFromRow read loaded_cost. 4) lib/field/sendChecks.ts / latestByTier: treat an approval whose cost no longer covers as 'none', so the phone offers Request approval again. Tests that fail before and pass after, in lib/pricing/policy.test.ts: 'an owner approval does not cover the same price after a line-hours override raises the cost' (seed fixture Good $3,500, hours x4 -> canSendQuote(...).ok false, problem below_floor) and 'an owner over-limit approval (belowFloor false) does not cover a below-floor problem at the same price' (Good $4,500, hours x3 -> ok false). Keep the existing test that the same cost still passes.

verdicts.reproduction: This step does not allow reading production, so I did not query it. I built a production-shaped database from tests/sql/00_supabase_stub.sql plus every file in supabase/migrations at 587ce69 (koala_revb_db) and exported app_settings to rows.json (22 keys). No migration on origin/main or the branch seeds default_state: grep default_state supabase/migrations/*.sql matches only the sync function's read at accuracy.sql:232. warranty_text is seeded in 20261020000002_phase1.sql:17 as 'Workmanship warranty — PLACEHOLDER, owner to replace.'. A scratch vitest (zz-b3.test.ts, removed afterwards) using the branch's consent.ts, profile.ts and settings.ts printed: 'keys 22 default_state= ""', 'gaps today: branding.license, branding.phone, default_state, warranty_text', 'consent THROWS: Not a US state: ', 'warranty on the document: "Workmanship warranty — PLACEHOLDER, owner to replace."', 'company: Koala Insulation of Newark | license: null | phone: null'. The call site is app/api/quotes/route.ts line 189: consent: esignConsent(profileValue(settingRows, 'default_state')), with the comment 'The state is in the profile (no gaps above)'. The throw is inside the try, so with the gate removed POST /api/quotes answers 500. quoteSettingsFromRows passes warranty_text through untouched; only isGap in profile.ts filters PLACEHOLDER. If the gate is removed as it stands, every send fails on a database like production's (estimators stuck, so high), and the PLACEHOLDER warranty prints on the page, the PDF and the email instead of 'Limited lifetime warranty'. verdicts.fixSpec: lib/quotes/consent.ts: add a state-free sentence (for example esignConsent(null) -> '... (ESIGN Act) ...', or name the property's state from draft.property.state when it is a real state), and never throw on a missing or invalid state. In route.ts use that instead of profileValue(settingRows,'default_state'). lib/quotes/settings.ts: make DEFAULT_WARRANTY 'Limited lifetime warranty', and treat an empty warranty_text or one matching /placeholder/i as unset (use the default). Optionally add an additive migration: update app_settings set value = '"Limited lifetime warranty"' where key = 'warranty_text' and value #>> '{}' = 'Workmanship warranty — PLACEHOLDER, owner to replace.' (conditional, hard rule 2). When the gate (businessProfileGaps check, 409 setup_incomplete) is removed, keep these. verdicts.reproduction: On my stack I inserted an estimate owned by the estimator (22222222-...) with SQL. verdicts.reasoning: The price_approvals_ask policy checks role, asker, pending and can_edit_estimate, but nothing about what is asked. A made-up model price cannot be used to send, because approvalCovers matches the server's model price, so the harm is a misled decider and queue spam, not a direct bypass. Medium.
